source_review.notes: Reviewed Princeton's Union-Find case study, lecture notes, and current UF API; maintained petgraph, NetworkX, and LLVM implementations; and current Illinois/Stanford academic algorithm materials. All eight final destinations returned HTTP 200. Two stale draft destinations returning 404 were replaced before review.

evidence: Checked universe U, partition Pi, equivalence relation, parent P, root size S, representative R, component count C, n, m, depth, height, and alpha notation.
Checked abstract blocks, external keys, dense indices, internal roots, stable component IDs, physical topology, logical snapshots, and durable versions remain distinct.
notation_and_syntax.notes: The inverse Ackermann function is described as asymptotically nonconstant and tied to the classical analysis convention.

evidence: Recomputed ten singleton components and eight successful balanced unions leaving exactly two components of sizes eight and two.
Recomputed path 7->6->4->0 at depth three and its reduction to depth one after full compression.
Recomputed redundant union(3,7) leaves count and size unchanged, while union(9,7) produces one component of size ten.
Recomputed Exercise 1 parent arrays and the size-doubling implications for depth five requiring at least 32 members.
numerical_recomputation.notes: Python exact integers do not test fixed-width size/count/byte overflow.

evidence: Verified root-to-root linking joins exactly two trees without a cycle and redundant union preserves the partition.
Verified path compression redirects only to ancestors in the same tree and therefore preserves equivalence, root size, and component count.
Verified the union-by-size height bound: every depth increase at least doubles containing-set size, yielding floor(log2 n).
Checked the sequence-level O(m alpha(n)) claim is conditional on union by rank/size plus path compression and is not a per-operation constant bound.
Verified ordinary DSU's monotone merge state cannot directly answer deletions/splits.
symbolic_recomputation.notes: The chapter distinguishes forest correctness, logarithmic weighting, and the stronger amortized theorem as separate claims.

evidence: Reviewed n=0, singleton, self/repeated/reversed union, all isolated/all connected, first/last/out-of-range indices, balanced and long legal paths.

Reviewed parent cycles, negative-to-unsigned conversion, recursive stack exhaustion, dynamic-map flooding, count/size/aggregate overflow, stale handles, generation reuse, and unbounded enumeration/history.

Reviewed aggregate failure, rollback/compression conflict, CSR-like array publication, concurrent opposing-root cycles, lost metadata, CAS retry/livelock, crash ordering, and unauthorized cross-tenant unions.
boundary_and_adversarial_cases.notes: Hostile persistent parents require bounds plus independent cycle/root/size/count validation before live find operations.

evidence: The executable validates every parent range, root termination/no repeated interior node, distinct root count, and independently recomputed size at each root.
The trace checks successful and redundant union behavior, component groups, root size, full compression, and final all-root parent state.
Reference-model guidance canonicalizes logical partitions so different valid representatives and topologies compare correctly.
invariant_checking.notes: The finite validator covers dense sequential union by size with full compression, not rollback, potentials, external maps, concurrency, or persistence.

evidence: Reviewed abstract partition, fixed/dynamic universe, forest representation, root-only union, size/rank distinctions, find variants, and sequence-bound interpretation.
Reviewed aggregates and fallible combination, weighted/potential variants, Kruskal and incremental connectivity boundaries, enumeration, rollback, offline deletions, and persistence choices.

Reviewed concurrency orientation/CAS/metadata/publication concerns, security boundaries, stable authorization identity, reference partitions, metamorphic tests, failure injection, and sequence benchmarks.
proof_review.notes: No correctness or optimality of an application such as Kruskal is inferred solely from DSU correctness.

evidence: The chapter labels the root-link partition proof, compression-preservation argument, size-doubling proof, and cited classical amortized result separately.
Finite topology evidence is explicitly not the inverse-Ackermann proof or concurrency/rollback/persistence evidence.
Maintained library behavior and academic claims are attached to named references; engineering alternatives are stated conditionally.
proof_sketch_labeling.notes: Root identity and near-constant practical behavior are not promoted to universal semantic or worst-case guarantees.

evidence: The standard-library-only Python trace passed exact sixteen-line stdout, empty stderr, and zero exit status under the recorded Python toolchain.
It emits evidence=finite_disjoint_set_forest_trace and demonstrates a depth-three path, compression, redundancy, grouping, final merge, and invariant validation.
All eight final external destinations returned HTTP 200 and all repository-local links passed module validation.
empirical_evidence_labeling.notes: No large-scale complexity, fixed-width failure, external-map, rollback, weighted relation, concurrent, crash, security, cache, or tail-latency behavior was empirically evaluated.

conceptual_review.notes: Reviewed partition semantics, forest invariants, weighted union, compression variants, amortization boundaries, metadata, monotone applications, rollback, concurrency, persistence, security, and evidence as a coherent system.

practitioner_review.notes: Reviewed external-key ownership, absent/duplicate admission, stable IDs, deterministic ties, aggregate failure/overflow, component enumeration, rollback histories, concurrent root orientation, publication/lifetime, versioned serialization, hostile loaders, resource limits, and sequence-based telemetry.

pedagogical_review.notes: Begins with the abstract partition, derives root linking and size doubling before inverse-Ackermann claims, includes a reproduced finite trace, ten contrasting examples, and five progressive exercises with complete answers.

limitations: Internal authoring, official/academic-source, mathematical, executable-snippet, conceptual, practitioner, and pedagogical evidence only; no external academic, Princeton, Stanford, Illinois, petgraph, NetworkX, LLVM, security, performance, reliability, operations, architecture, or independent practitioner review is claimed. The chapter and finite trace prove neither all disjoint-set implementations, the classical amortized theorem from first principles, arbitrary external mappings or metadata, fixed-width/allocation/failure safety, weighted/potential constraints, rollback or persistent versions, online deletion, thread safety/linearizability/lock freedom, safe publication/reclamation, durable crash recovery, hostile-loader security, production cache/contention/tail behavior, certification, nor deployment fitness.
